title: Claude identifies a new enzyme system: array-associated reverse transcriptases
summary: About 950 Claude agents searched a DNA-sequence database for 21 hours (210 million tokens) and flagged an uncharacterized enzyme system, found mostly in bacteriophages, with a DNA repeat array similar to CRISPR. Scientists performed the laboratory work; the function remains unknown, and the work is a preprint, not a peer-reviewed publication.

evidence.tested: Human scientists expressed the protein in laboratory strains and characterized it biochemically and structurally; early experiments showed the array is expressed as distinct short RNAs.
evidence.unknown: The primary function of the enzyme system is unknown; findings are preliminary, and most Claude-proposed candidates are eliminated in follow-up review.
evidence.ai_role: About 950 agents used 210 million tokens over 21 hours to search DNA sequences, narrowing about 3,500 candidate systems to 20; one agent noticed the repeat array and filed a report.
